title: fix(memory): preserve selected plugin casing for dreaming sidecars
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a selected external memory plugin with a mixed-case declared ID can serve recall while its explicitly requested bundled dreaming sidecar is missing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the declared runtime ID in both dreaming authorization owners: startup planning/metadata and scoped runtime loading. Reuse the existing slot normalizer rather than lowercasing manifest identity. Existing enablement, deny, explicit-disable and memory-kind authorization remain authoritative.

## User Impact

User impact: the configured dreaming intent capability is available alongside a mixed-case selected memory plugin, as it already is for an equivalent lowercase ID. Disabling dreaming continues to leave that sidecar unavailable.

## Evidence

- Scenario: Mixed-case selected memory ID retains its requested dreaming sidecar; Lowercase recall and disabled-dreaming controls preserve existing behavior
- Entry: Normally built openclaw.mjs gateway run; public sessions.create, plugins.list and tools.invoke memory_get/intent with a declared external memory fixture and actual bundled memory-core; disputed owner ran unmocked: src/plugins/gateway-startup-plugin-config.ts and src/plugins/loader-shared.ts, reached by normal Gateway plugin startup and public tools.invoke
- Same command on base `b3d0977` and head `5499714`: `node proof-memory-case.mjs CHECKOUT NEW_OUTPUT base|head`
  - Before (base): RED: selected Proof-Memory memory_get returns its sentinel, but the requested bundled intent tool is not found. The otherwise identical lowercase proof-memory selection exposes intent and returns intents=[].
  - After (head): GREEN: the same mixed-case selection exposes both selected memory_get and the bundled intent tool, returning the actual empty intent list through public tools.invoke.
- Readback (websocket): External public WebSocket client records actual selected recall sentinel, bundled intent details and plugin inventory from the normally built Gateway.
- Proof harness: https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/8ac0d8554b8c29e1e11283364b2e571a5ae75192/OC/proof/2026-11-03-distinct-families
- Control: Authoritative tools.invoke returns 0 available intent tools for mixed-case base and 1 for the same mixed-case head. Positive lowercase control returns 1 on both versions; disabled-dreaming control returns 0 on both. Selected memory_get returns its sentinel in all 6 scenario/version combinations.
- Other callers checked: Both startup plan and startup metadata share the repaired startup owner; scoped loader authorization/source identity uses the repaired runtime owner. Canonical policy normalization, allow/deny/disabled gates, blank/none slot semantics and cache provenance remain with existing owners. Existing owner suites and a focused startup sibling retain these controls.
- Tests: pnpm test src/plugins/provider-hook-runtime.provenance.test.ts src/plugins/channel-plugin-ids.test.ts src/plugins/gateway-startup-plugin-plan.memory-sidecar.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 (measured cost: 138 passed across 3 files; owner-suite process 176.51s wall. Full check costs are disclosed below.)
- Not tested: Scheduled dreaming execution, actual model output, installed third-party packages, Windows/macOS, installed-release upgrades and exact-head hosted CI were not run locally. The external plugin is a normal declared synthetic recall fixture; the bundled sidecar is real. Proof covers startup and tool availability, not dreaming quality or scheduling.

[Inspectable collector and paired public-entry readback](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/tree/8ac0d8554b8c29e1e11283364b2e571a5ae75192/OC/proof/2026-11-03-distinct-families/memory-sidecar-case-readback.json). Product head `5499714ddda0c86e644cd38b8b575ef9a04b8375`.

<details>
<summary>Validation and scope</summary>

Normal source build, commit hooks, formatting, ordinary typed lint, targeted types and test-line ratchet passed; 138 passed across 3 files. Independent gpt6.1-sol adversarial review covered the complete production/test/allocation diff from `b3d0977b0cc484c4b472628385d1a988a794ac42` to `5499714ddda0c86e644cd38b8b575ef9a04b8375` (tree `c8304674615a06c07d3ce5662b3ce94106a04239`), with zero findings, using the user-authorized fallback for unavailable official autoreview.

Outer process wall times: format 0.36s (exit 0); lint 26.79s (exit 0); types 20.06s (exit 0); test-lines 14.21s (exit 0); tests 176.51s (exit 0).

File additions/deletions:

```text
2	0	config/test-lines-allocations/alix-memory-sidecar-case-20261103.txt
1	3	src/plugins/gateway-startup-plugin-config.ts
35	0	src/plugins/gateway-startup-plugin-plan.memory-sidecar.test.ts
4	11	src/plugins/loader-shared.ts
36	33	src/plugins/provider-hook-runtime.provenance.test.ts
```

Existing-solutions preflight: This restores the existing selected-memory sidecar contract; changing a declared plugin ID is not a substitute for preserving runtime identity. Both affected authorization producers are fixed together. No permission or selection policy is added. All-state semantic and changed-file competitor scans and Alix/Leon open-file checks found no viable competing fix.

No new config/defaults, schema/protocol, security/permissions, database format or migration. All fixture state is isolated; owned processes are joined. No production service, external channel or model was used.

Scheduled dreaming execution, actual model output, installed third-party packages, Windows/macOS, installed-release upgrades and exact-head hosted CI were not run locally. The external plugin is a normal declared synthetic recall fixture; the bundled sidecar is real. Proof covers startup and tool availability, not dreaming quality or scheduling.

</details>
